[223](#223)fn generate_upcaster_tokens(
[224](#224)    owner: &Ident,
[225](#225)    upcasters: &[UpcasterDef],
[226](#226)) -> (proc_macro2::TokenStream, proc_macro2::TokenStream) {
[227](#227)    if upcasters.is_empty() {
[228](#228)        return (quote! {}, quote! {});
[229](#229)    }
[230](#230)
[231](#231)    let prefix = upcaster_wrapper_prefix(owner);
[232](#232)    let wrapper_names: Vec<_> = upcasters
[233](#233)        .iter()
[234](#234)        .enumerate()
[235](#235)        .map(|(idx, _)| format_ident!("__sourced_upcast_{}_{}", prefix, idx))
[236](#236)        .collect();
[237](#237)
[238](#238)    let wrapper_defs = upcasters
[239](#239)        .iter()
[240](#240)        .zip(wrapper_names.iter())
[241](#241)        .map(|(u, wrapper)| {
[242](#242)            let source_type = &u.source_type;
[243](#243)            let target_type = &u.target_type;
[244](#244)            let to_version = &u.to_version;
[245](#245)            let transform_fn = &u.transform_fn;
[246](#246)            quote! {
[247](#247)                fn #wrapper(
[248](#248)                    event: &distributed::EventRecord,
[249](#249)                ) -> Result<Vec<u8>, distributed::UpcastError> {
[250](#250)                    distributed::upcast_payload::<#source_type, #target_type>(
[251](#251)                        event,
[252](#252)                        #to_version,
[253](#253)                        #transform_fn,
[254](#254)                    )
[255](#255)                }
[256](#256)            }
[257](#257)        });
[258](#258)
[259](#259)    let upcaster_entries = upcasters
[260](#260)        .iter()
[261](#261)        .zip(wrapper_names.iter())
[262](#262)        .map(|(u, wrapper)| {
[263](#263)            let event_name = &u.event_name;
[264](#264)            let from_version = &u.from_version;
[265](#265)            let to_version = &u.to_version;
[266](#266)            quote! {
[267](#267)                distributed::EventUpcaster {
[268](#268)                    event_type: #event_name,
[269](#269)                    from_version: #from_version,
[270](#270)                    to_version: #to_version,
[271](#271)                    transform: #owner::#wrapper,
[272](#272)                }
[273](#273)            }
[274](#274)        });
[275](#275)
[276](#276)    let upcasters_method = quote! {
[277](#277)        fn upcasters() -> &'static [distributed::EventUpcaster] {
[278](#278)            static UPCASTERS: &[distributed::EventUpcaster] = &[
[279](#279)                #(#upcaster_entries),*
[280](#280)            ];
[281](#281)            UPCASTERS
[282](#282)        }
[283](#283)    };
[284](#284)
[285](#285)    (
[286](#286)        quote! {
[287](#287)            impl #owner {
[288](#288)                #(#wrapper_defs)*
[289](#289)            }
[290](#290)        },
[291](#291)        upcasters_method,
[292](#292)    )
[293](#293)}

[354](#354)fn expand_enqueue(attr: TokenStream2, item: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
[355](#355)    let args = parse_enqueue_args.parse2(attr)?;
[356](#356)    let mut func = syn::parse2::<ItemFn>(item)?;
[357](#357)
[358](#358)    let signature_synthesized = ensure_sourced_result_signature(&mut func.sig, "enqueue")?;
[359](#359)
[360](#360)    let emitter_field = &args.emitter_field;
[361](#361)    let event_name = &args.event_name;
[362](#362)
[363](#363)    let params = extract_params_with_types(&func.sig, "enqueue")?;
[365](#365)    let param_names: Vec<&Ident> = params.iter().map(|(name, _)| name).collect();
[366](#366)
[367](#367)    let entity_field = &args.entity_field;
[368](#368)
[369](#369)    let enqueue_call = if param_names.is_empty() {
[370](#370)        quote! {
[371](#371)            if !self.#entity_field.is_replaying() {
[372](#372)                self.#emitter_field.enqueue(#event_name, "");
[373](#373)            };
[374](#374)        }
[375](#375)    } else if param_names.len() == 1 {
[376](#376)        let param = ¶m_names[0];
[378](#378)        quote! {
[379](#379)            if !self.#entity_field.is_replaying() {
[380](#380)                self.#emitter_field.enqueue_with(#event_name, &(#param.clone(),))?;
[381](#381)            };
[382](#382)        }
[383](#383)    } else {
[384](#384)        quote! {
[386](#386)            if !self.#entity_field.is_replaying() {
[387](#387)                self.#emitter_field.enqueue_with(#event_name, &(#(#param_names.clone()),*))?;
[388](#388)            };
[389](#389)        }
[390](#390)    };
[391](#391)
[392](#392)    let new_body = wrap_result_body_with_guard(
[393](#393)        args.guard.as_ref(),
[394](#394)        enqueue_call,
[395](#395)        &func.block,
[396](#396)        signature_synthesized,
[397](#397)    );
[398](#398)    *func.block = new_body;
[399](#399)
[400](#400)    Ok(quote! { #func })
[401](#401)}

[403](#403)struct EnqueueArgs {
[404](#404)    emitter_field: syn::Ident,
[405](#405)    entity_field: syn::Ident,
[406](#406)    event_name: LitStr,
[407](#407)    guard: Option<Expr>,
[408](#408)}
[409](#409)
[410](#410)fn parse_enqueue_args(input: syn::parse::ParseStream) -> syn::Result<EnqueueArgs> {
[411](#411)    let (emitter_field, event_name) = if input.peek(LitStr) {
[413](#413)        let event_name: LitStr = input.parse()?;
[415](#415)        (format_ident!("emitter"), event_name)
[416](#416)    } else {
[417](#417)        let first_ident: syn::Ident = input.parse()?;
[419](#419)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[420](#420)        let event_name: LitStr = input.parse()?;
[421](#421)        (first_ident, event_name)
[422](#422)    };
[423](#423)
[424](#424)    let mut guard = None;
[425](#425)    let mut entity_field = format_ident!("entity");
[428](#428)
[429](#429)    while input.peek(Token![,]) {
[431](#431)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[432](#432)        if input.is_empty() {
[434](#434)            break;
[435](#435)        }
[436](#436)        let ident: syn::Ident = input.parse()?;
[437](#437)        if ident == "when" {
[438](#438)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[439](#439)            guard = Some(input.parse()?);
[440](#440)        } else if ident == "entity" {
[441](#441)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[442](#442)            entity_field = input.parse()?;
[443](#443)        } else {
[444](#444)            return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[445](#445)                &ident,
[446](#446)                format!(
[447](#447)                    "unsupported key `{ident}` in #[enqueue(...)]; expected `when` or `entity`"
[448](#448)                ),
[449](#449)            ));
[450](#450)        }
[451](#451)    }
[452](#452)
[453](#453)    Ok(EnqueueArgs {
[454](#454)        emitter_field,
[455](#455)        entity_field,
[456](#456)        event_name,
[457](#457)        guard,
[458](#458)    })
[459](#459)}

[521](#521)pub fn digest(attr: TokenStream, item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {

[524](#524)        .into()
[525](#525)}

[527](#527)fn expand_digest(attr: TokenStream2, item: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
[528](#528)    let args = parse_digest_args.parse2(attr)?;
[529](#529)    let mut func = syn::parse2::<ItemFn>(item)?;
[530](#530)
[531](#531)    let signature_synthesized = ensure_sourced_result_signature(&mut func.sig, "digest")?;
[532](#532)
[533](#533)    let params = extract_params_with_types(&func.sig, "digest")?;
[534](#534)    let param_names: Vec<&Ident> = params.iter().map(|(name, _)| name).collect();
[535](#535)    let digest_call = generate_digest_call(
[536](#536)        &args.entity_field,
[537](#537)        &args.event_name,
[538](#538)        ¶m_names,
[539](#539)        args.version.as_ref(),
[540](#540)    );
[541](#541)
[542](#542)    let new_body = wrap_result_body_with_guard(
[543](#543)        args.guard.as_ref(),
[544](#544)        digest_call,
[545](#545)        &func.block,
[546](#546)        signature_synthesized,
[547](#547)    );
[548](#548)    *func.block = new_body;
[549](#549)
[550](#550)    Ok(quote! { #func })
[551](#551)}
[552](#552)
[553](#553)struct DigestArgs {
[554](#554)    entity_field: syn::Ident,
[555](#555)    event_name: LitStr,
[556](#556)    guard: Option<Expr>,
[557](#557)    version: Option<syn::LitInt>,
[558](#558)}
[559](#559)
[560](#560)fn parse_digest_args(input: syn::parse::ParseStream) -> syn::Result<DigestArgs> {
[561](#561)    let (entity_field, event_name) = if input.peek(LitStr) {
[563](#563)        let event_name: LitStr = input.parse()?;
[565](#565)        (format_ident!("entity"), event_name)
[566](#566)    } else {
[567](#567)        let first_ident: syn::Ident = input.parse()?;
[569](#569)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[570](#570)        let event_name: LitStr = input.parse()?;
[571](#571)        (first_ident, event_name)
[572](#572)    };
[573](#573)
[574](#574)    let mut guard = None;
[575](#575)    let mut version = None;
[576](#576)
[577](#577)    while input.peek(Token![,]) {
[579](#579)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[580](#580)        if input.is_empty() {
[582](#582)            break;
[583](#583)        }
[584](#584)        let ident: syn::Ident = input.parse()?;
[585](#585)        if ident == "when" {
[586](#586)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[587](#587)            guard = Some(input.parse()?);
[588](#588)        } else if ident == "version" {
[589](#589)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[590](#590)            version = Some(input.parse()?);
[591](#591)        } else {
[592](#592)            return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[593](#593)                &ident,
[594](#594)                format!(
[595](#595)                    "unsupported key `{ident}` in #[digest(...)]; expected `when` or `version`"
[596](#596)                ),
[597](#597)            ));
[598](#598)        }
[599](#599)    }
[600](#600)
[601](#601)    Ok(DigestArgs {
[602](#602)        entity_field,
[603](#603)        event_name,
[604](#604)        guard,
[605](#605)        version,
[606](#606)    })

[608](#608)
[609](#609)fn aggregate_impl_tokens(
[622](#622)    type_name: &Ident,
[623](#623)    entity_field: &Ident,
[624](#624)    aggregate_type_method: &Option<TokenStream2>,
[625](#625)    replay_arms: &[TokenStream2],
[626](#626)    upcasters_method: &TokenStream2,
[627](#627)) -> TokenStream2 {
[628](#628)    quote! {
[629](#629)        impl distributed::Aggregate for #type_name {
[630](#630)            type ReplayError = String;
[631](#631)
[632](#632)            #aggregate_type_method
[633](#633)
[634](#634)            fn entity(&self) -> &distributed::Entity {
[635](#635)                &self.#entity_field
[636](#636)            }
[637](#637)
[638](#638)            fn entity_mut(&mut self) -> &mut distributed::Entity {
[639](#639)                &mut self.#entity_field
[640](#640)            }
[641](#641)
[642](#642)            fn replay_event(
[643](#643)                &mut self,
[644](#644)                event: &distributed::EventRecord,
[645](#645)            ) -> Result<(), Self::ReplayError> {
[646](#646)                match event.event_name.as_str() {
[647](#647)                    #(#replay_arms)*
[648](#648)                    _ => return Err(format!("Unknown event: {}", event.event_name)),
[649](#649)                }
[650](#650)                Ok(())
[651](#651)            }
[652](#652)
[653](#653)            #upcasters_method
[654](#654)        }
[655](#655)    }

[679](#679)pub fn aggregate(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {

[681](#681)        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.to_compile_error())
[682](#682)        .into()

[684](#684)
[685](#685)fn expand_aggregate(input: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
[686](#686)    let input = syn::parse2::<AggregateInput>(input)?;
[687](#687)
[688](#688)    let agg_name = &input.agg_name;
[689](#689)    let entity_field = &input.entity_field;
[690](#690)
[691](#691)    let replay_arms: Vec<_> = input
[693](#693)        .events
[694](#694)        .iter()
[695](#695)        .map(|evt| {
[696](#696)            let event_name = &evt.event_name;
[697](#697)            let method_name = &evt.method_name;
[698](#698)            let args = &evt.args;
[699](#699)
[700](#700)            let call_args: Vec<_> = match &evt.method_args {
[702](#702)                Some(method_args) => method_args.clone(),
[703](#703)                None => args.clone(),
[704](#704)            };
[705](#705)
[706](#706)            if args.is_empty() {
[707](#707)                quote! {
[709](#709)                    #event_name => {
[710](#710)                        self.#method_name().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[711](#711)                    }
[712](#712)                }
[713](#713)            } else if call_args.is_empty() {
[714](#714)                quote! {
[716](#716)                    #event_name => {
[717](#717)                        self.#method_name().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[718](#718)                    }
[719](#719)                }
[720](#720)            } else if args.len() == 1 {
[721](#721)                let arg = &args[0];
[723](#723)                let call_arg = &call_args[0];
[724](#724)                quote! {
[725](#725)                    #event_name => {
[726](#726)                        let (#arg,) = event.decode().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[727](#727)                        self.#method_name(#call_arg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[728](#728)                    }
[729](#729)                }
[730](#730)            } else {
[731](#731)                quote! {
[733](#733)                    #event_name => {
[734](#734)                        let (#(#args),*) = event.decode().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[735](#735)                        self.#method_name(#(#call_args),*).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[736](#736)                    }
[737](#737)                }
[738](#738)            }
[739](#739)        })
[740](#740)        .collect();
[741](#741)
[742](#742)    let (upcaster_wrappers, upcasters_method) =
[743](#743)        generate_upcaster_tokens(agg_name, &input.upcasters);
[744](#744)    let aggregate_type_method = input.aggregate_type.as_ref().map(|aggregate_type| {
[745](#745)        quote! {
[746](#746)            fn aggregate_type() -> &'static str {
[747](#747)                #aggregate_type
[748](#748)            }
[749](#749)        }
[750](#750)    });
[751](#751)
[752](#752)    let aggregate_impl = aggregate_impl_tokens(
[758](#758)        agg_name,
[759](#759)        entity_field,
[760](#760)        &aggregate_type_method,
[761](#761)        &replay_arms,
[762](#762)        &upcasters_method,
[763](#763)    );
[764](#764)    let expanded = quote! {
[765](#765)        #upcaster_wrappers
[766](#766)
[767](#767)        #aggregate_impl
[768](#768)    };
[769](#769)
[770](#770)    Ok(expanded)
[771](#771)}

[837](#837)struct EventDef {
[838](#838)    event_name: LitStr,
[839](#839)    args: Vec<Ident>,
[840](#840)    method_name: Ident,
[841](#841)    method_args: Option<Vec<Ident>>, }
[843](#843)
[844](#844)fn validate_aggregate_type_literal(lit: &LitStr) -> syn::Result<()> {
[845](#845)    let value = lit.value();
[846](#846)    if value.trim().is_empty() {
[847](#847)        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[848](#848)            lit,
[849](#849)            "`aggregate_type` must not be empty or whitespace",
[850](#850)        ));
[851](#851)    }
[852](#852)    if value.contains('\u{1f}') {
[853](#853)        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[854](#854)            lit,
[855](#855)            "`aggregate_type` must not contain the reserved stream delimiter (U+001F)",
[856](#856)        ));
[857](#857)    }
[858](#858)    Ok(())
[859](#859)}
[860](#860)
[861](#861)impl Parse for AggregateInput {
[862](#862)    fn parse(input: ParseStream) -> syn::Result<Self> {
[863](#863)        let agg_name: Ident = input.parse()?;
[864](#864)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[865](#865)        let entity_field: Ident = input.parse()?;
[866](#866)        let mut aggregate_type = None;
[867](#867)
[868](#868)        if input.peek(Token![,]) {
[869](#869)            input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[870](#870)            let kw: Ident = input.parse()?;
[871](#871)            if kw != "aggregate_type" {
[872](#872)                return Err(syn::Error::new(kw.span(), "expected `aggregate_type`"));
[873](#873)            }
[874](#874)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[875](#875)            let lit = input.parse::<LitStr>()?;
[876](#876)            validate_aggregate_type_literal(&lit)?;
[877](#877)            aggregate_type = Some(lit);
[878](#878)        }
[879](#879)
[880](#880)        let content;
[881](#881)        braced!(content in input);
[882](#882)
[883](#883)        let mut events = Vec::new();
[884](#884)        while !content.is_empty() {
[885](#885)            let event_name: LitStr = content.parse()?;
[886](#886)
[887](#887)            let args_content;
[889](#889)            syn::parenthesized!(args_content in content);
[890](#890)            let args: syn::punctuated::Punctuated<Ident, Token![,]> =
[891](#891)                args_content.parse_terminated(Ident::parse, Token![,])?;
[892](#892)            let args: Vec<Ident> = args.into_iter().collect();
[893](#893)
[894](#894)            content.parse::<Token![=>]>()?;
[895](#895)            let method_name: Ident = content.parse()?;
[896](#896)
[897](#897)            let method_args = if content.peek(syn::token::Paren) {
[899](#899)                let method_args_content;
[900](#900)                syn::parenthesized!(method_args_content in content);
[901](#901)                let method_args: syn::punctuated::Punctuated<Ident, Token![,]> =
[902](#902)                    method_args_content.parse_terminated(Ident::parse, Token![,])?;
[903](#903)                Some(method_args.into_iter().collect())
[904](#904)            } else {
[905](#905)                None };
[907](#907)
[908](#908)            events.push(EventDef {
[909](#909)                event_name,
[910](#910)                args,
[911](#911)                method_name,
[912](#912)                method_args,
[913](#913)            });
[914](#914)
[915](#915)            if content.peek(Token![,]) {
[917](#917)                content.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[918](#918)            }
[919](#919)        }
[920](#920)
[921](#921)        let mut upcasters = Vec::new();
[923](#923)        if input.peek(syn::Ident) {
[924](#924)            let kw: Ident = input.parse()?;
[925](#925)            if kw != "upcasters" {
[926](#926)                return Err(syn::Error::new(kw.span(), "expected `upcasters`"));
[927](#927)            }
[928](#928)
[929](#929)            let upcaster_content;
[930](#930)            syn::bracketed!(upcaster_content in input);
[931](#931)            upcasters = parse_upcaster_list(&upcaster_content)?;
[932](#932)        }
[933](#933)
[934](#934)        Ok(AggregateInput {
[935](#935)            agg_name,
[936](#936)            entity_field,
[937](#937)            aggregate_type,
[938](#938)            events,
[939](#939)            upcasters,
[940](#940)        })
[941](#941)    }
[942](#942)}

[944](#944)struct SourcedArgs {
[949](#949)    entity_field: Ident,
[950](#950)    enum_name: Option<LitStr>,
[951](#951)    aggregate_type: Option<LitStr>,
[952](#952)    enqueue: Option<Ident>, upcasters: Vec<UpcasterDef>,
[954](#954)}
[955](#955)
[956](#956)fn parse_sourced_args(input: ParseStream) -> syn::Result<SourcedArgs> {
[957](#957)    if input.is_empty() {
[958](#958)        return Err(
[959](#959)            input.error("#[sourced] requires the entity field name, e.g. `#[sourced(entity)]`")
[960](#960)        );
[961](#961)    }
[962](#962)    let entity_field: Ident = input.parse()?;
[963](#963)    let mut enum_name = None;
[964](#964)    let mut aggregate_type = None;
[965](#965)    let mut enqueue = None;
[966](#966)    let mut upcasters = Vec::new();
[967](#967)
[968](#968)    while input.peek(Token![,]) {
[969](#969)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[970](#970)        if input.is_empty() {
[972](#972)            break;
[973](#973)        }
[974](#974)        let kw: Ident = input.parse()?;
[975](#975)        if kw == "events" {
[976](#976)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[977](#977)            enum_name = Some(input.parse::<LitStr>()?);
[978](#978)        } else if kw == "aggregate_type" {
[979](#979)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[980](#980)            let lit = input.parse::<LitStr>()?;
[981](#981)            validate_aggregate_type_literal(&lit)?;
[982](#982)            aggregate_type = Some(lit);
[983](#983)        } else if kw == "enqueue" {
[984](#984)            if input.peek(syn::token::Paren) {
[986](#986)                let inner;
[987](#987)                syn::parenthesized!(inner in input);
[988](#988)                enqueue = Some(inner.parse::<Ident>()?);
[989](#989)            } else {
[990](#990)                enqueue = Some(format_ident!("emitter"));
[991](#991)            }
[992](#992)        } else if kw == "upcasters" {
[993](#993)            let upcaster_content;
[994](#994)            syn::parenthesized!(upcaster_content in input);
[995](#995)            upcasters = parse_upcaster_list(&upcaster_content)?;
[996](#996)        } else {
[997](#997)            return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[998](#998)                &kw,
[999](#999)                format!(
[1000](#1000)                    "unsupported key `{kw}` in #[sourced(...)]; expected `events`, `aggregate_type`, `enqueue`, or `upcasters`"
[1001](#1001)                ),
[1002](#1002)            ));
[1003](#1003)        }
[1004](#1004)    }
[1005](#1005)
[1006](#1006)    Ok(SourcedArgs {
[1007](#1007)        entity_field,
[1008](#1008)        enum_name,
[1009](#1009)        aggregate_type,
[1010](#1010)        enqueue,
[1011](#1011)        upcasters,
[1012](#1012)    })
[1013](#1013)}
[1014](#1014)
[1015](#1015)struct EventAttr {

[1018](#1018)    version: Option<syn::LitInt>,
[1019](#1019)}
[1020](#1020)
[1021](#1021)fn parse_event_args(input: ParseStream) -> syn::Result<EventAttr> {
[1022](#1022)    let event_name: LitStr = input.parse()?;
[1023](#1023)    let mut guard = None;
[1024](#1024)    let mut version = None;
[1025](#1025)
[1026](#1026)    while input.peek(Token![,]) {
[1027](#1027)        input.parse::<Token![,]>()?;
[1028](#1028)        if input.is_empty() {
[1030](#1030)            break;
[1031](#1031)        }
[1032](#1032)        let ident: Ident = input.parse()?;
[1033](#1033)        if ident == "when" {
[1034](#1034)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[1035](#1035)            guard = Some(input.parse()?);
[1036](#1036)        } else if ident == "version" {
[1037](#1037)            input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[1038](#1038)            version = Some(input.parse()?);
[1039](#1039)        } else {
[1040](#1040)            return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[1041](#1041)                &ident,
[1042](#1042)                format!("unsupported key `{ident}` in #[event(...)]; expected `when` or `version`"),
[1043](#1043)            ));
[1044](#1044)        }
[1045](#1045)    }
[1046](#1046)
[1047](#1047)    Ok(EventAttr {
[1048](#1048)        event_name,
[1049](#1049)        guard,
[1050](#1050)        version,
[1051](#1051)    })

[1053](#1053)
[1054](#1054)fn find_and_remove_event_attr(
[1055](#1055)    attrs: &mut Vec<syn::Attribute>,
[1056](#1056)) -> Result<Option<EventAttr>, syn::Error> {
[1057](#1057)    let idx = attrs.iter().position(|a| a.path().is_ident("event"));
[1058](#1058)    match idx {
[1059](#1059)        Some(idx) => {
[1060](#1060)            let attr = attrs.remove(idx);
[1061](#1061)            let event_attr = attr.parse_args_with(parse_event_args)?;
[1062](#1062)            Ok(Some(event_attr))
[1063](#1063)        }
[1064](#1064)        None => Ok(None),
[1065](#1065)    }

[1074](#1074)#[proc_macro_attribute]
[1109](#1109)pub fn sourced(attr: TokenStream, item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[1110](#1110)    expand_sourced(attr.into(), item.into())
[1111](#1111)        .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.to_compile_error())
[1112](#1112)        .into()
[1113](#1113)}
[1114](#1114)
[1115](#1115)fn expand_sourced(attr: TokenStream2, item: TokenStream2) -> syn::Result<TokenStream2> {
[1116](#1116)    let args = parse_sourced_args.parse2(attr)?;
[1117](#1117)    let mut impl_block = syn::parse2::<ItemImpl>(item)?;
[1118](#1118)
[1119](#1119)    let struct_name = match &*impl_block.self_ty {
[1121](#1121)        syn::Type::Path(type_path) => match type_path.path.segments.last() {
[1122](#1122)            Some(segment) => segment.ident.clone(),
[1123](#1123)            None => {
[1124](#1124)                return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[1125](#1125)                    &impl_block.self_ty,
[1126](#1126)                    "#[sourced] requires a named type",
[1127](#1127)                ));
[1128](#1128)            }
[1129](#1129)        },
[1130](#1130)        _ => {
[1131](#1131)            return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[1132](#1132)                &impl_block.self_ty,
[1133](#1133)                "#[sourced] requires a named type",
[1134](#1134)            ));
[1135](#1135)        }
[1136](#1136)    };
[1137](#1137)
[1138](#1138)    let mut event_methods: Vec<EventMethodInfo> = Vec::new();
[1140](#1140)    let mut seen_events: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
[1143](#1143)    let mut seen_variants: std::collections::HashMap<String, LitStr> =
[1149](#1149)        std::collections::HashMap::new();
[1150](#1150)
[1151](#1151)    for item in &mut impl_block.items {
[1152](#1152)        if let syn::ImplItem::Fn(method) = item {
[1153](#1153)            match find_and_remove_event_attr(&mut method.attrs) {
[1154](#1154)                Ok(Some(event_attr)) => {
[1155](#1155)                    if !matches!(method.sig.inputs.first(), Some(FnArg::Receiver(_))) {
[1159](#1159)                        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[1160](#1160)                            &method.sig,
[1161](#1161)                            "#[event] methods must take a `&mut self` receiver",
[1162](#1162)                        ));
[1163](#1163)                    }
[1164](#1164)
[1165](#1165)                    let event_key = event_attr.event_name.value();
[1166](#1166)                    if !seen_events.insert(event_key.clone()) {
[1167](#1167)                        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[1168](#1168)                            &event_attr.event_name,
[1169](#1169)                            format!("duplicate #[event] name `{event_key}` in this #[sourced] impl block"),
[1170](#1170)                        ));
[1171](#1171)                    }
[1172](#1172)
[1173](#1173)                    let variant = event_variant_ident(&event_attr.event_name);
[1174](#1174)                    if let Some(prev) = seen_variants.get(&variant.to_string()) {
[1175](#1175)                        return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[1176](#1176)                            &event_attr.event_name,
[1177](#1177)                            format!(
[1178](#1178)                                "#[event] names `{}` and `{event_key}` both derive the enum variant `{variant}`; rename one so the variant names are distinct",
[1179](#1179)                                prev.value()
[1180](#1180)                            ),
[1181](#1181)                        ));
[1182](#1182)                    }
[1183](#1183)                    seen_variants.insert(variant.to_string(), event_attr.event_name.clone());
[1184](#1184)
[1185](#1185)                    let signature_synthesized =
[1186](#1186)                        ensure_sourced_result_signature(&mut method.sig, "event")?;
[1187](#1187)
[1188](#1188)                    let params = extract_params_with_types(&method.sig, "event")?;
[1189](#1189)                    let param_name_refs: Vec<&Ident> =
[1190](#1190)                        params.iter().map(|(name, _)| name).collect();
[1191](#1191)
[1192](#1192)                    let enqueue_call = args.enqueue.as_ref().map(|emitter_field| {
[1194](#1194)                        generate_enqueue_call(
[1195](#1195)                            &args.entity_field,
[1196](#1196)                            emitter_field,
[1197](#1197)                            &event_attr.event_name,
[1198](#1198)                            ¶m_name_refs,
[1199](#1199)                        )
[1200](#1200)                    });
[1201](#1201)                    let digest_call = generate_digest_call(
[1202](#1202)                        &args.entity_field,
[1203](#1203)                        &event_attr.event_name,
[1204](#1204)                        ¶m_name_refs,
[1205](#1205)                        event_attr.version.as_ref(),
[1206](#1206)                    );
[1207](#1207)                    let prepend = quote! {
[1208](#1208)                        #enqueue_call
[1209](#1209)                        #digest_call
[1210](#1210)                    };
[1211](#1211)
[1212](#1212)                    let new_body = wrap_result_body_with_guard(
[1213](#1213)                        event_attr.guard.as_ref(),
[1214](#1214)                        prepend,
[1215](#1215)                        &method.block,
[1216](#1216)                        signature_synthesized,
[1217](#1217)                    );
[1218](#1218)                    method.block = new_body;
[1219](#1219)
[1220](#1220)                    event_methods.push(EventMethodInfo {
[1221](#1221)                        event_name: event_attr.event_name,
[1222](#1222)                        method_name: method.sig.ident.clone(),
[1223](#1223)                        params,
[1224](#1224)                    });
[1225](#1225)                }
[1226](#1226)                Ok(None) => { }
[1227](#1227)                Err(err) => return Err(err),
[1228](#1228)            }
[1229](#1229)        }
[1230](#1230)    }
[1231](#1231)
[1232](#1232)    let enum_name = if let Some(ref custom) = args.enum_name {
[1234](#1234)        format_ident!("{}", custom.value())
[1235](#1235)    } else {
[1236](#1236)        format_ident!("{}Event", struct_name)
[1237](#1237)    };
[1238](#1238)
[1239](#1239)    let enum_variants = event_methods.iter().map(|e| {
[1241](#1241)        let variant_name = event_variant_ident(&e.event_name);
[1242](#1242)        if e.params.is_empty() {
[1243](#1243)            quote! { #variant_name }
[1244](#1244)        } else {
[1245](#1245)            let fields = e.params.iter().map(|(name, ty)| quote! { #name: #ty });
[1246](#1246)            quote! { #variant_name { #(#fields),* } }
[1247](#1247)        }
[1248](#1248)    });
[1249](#1249)
[1250](#1250)    let enum_def = quote! {
[1251](#1251)        #[allow(clippy::enum_variant_names)]
[1252](#1252)        #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
[1253](#1253)        pub enum #enum_name {
[1254](#1254)            #(#enum_variants),*
[1255](#1255)        }
[1256](#1256)    };
[1257](#1257)
[1258](#1258)    let event_name_arms = event_methods.iter().map(|e| {
[1260](#1260)        let variant_name = event_variant_ident(&e.event_name);
[1261](#1261)        let name_str = &e.event_name;
[1262](#1262)        if e.params.is_empty() {
[1263](#1263)            quote! { #enum_name::#variant_name => #name_str }
[1264](#1264)        } else {
[1265](#1265)            quote! { #enum_name::#variant_name { .. } => #name_str }
[1266](#1266)        }
[1267](#1267)    });
[1268](#1268)
[1269](#1269)    let event_name_impl = quote! {
[1270](#1270)        impl #enum_name {
[1271](#1271)            pub fn event_name(&self) -> &'static str {
[1272](#1272)                match self {
[1273](#1273)                    #(#event_name_arms),*
[1274](#1274)                }
[1275](#1275)            }
[1276](#1276)        }
[1277](#1277)    };
[1278](#1278)
[1279](#1279)    let try_from_arms = event_methods.iter().map(|e| {
[1281](#1281)        let variant_name = event_variant_ident(&e.event_name);
[1282](#1282)        let event_name_str = &e.event_name;
[1283](#1283)        if e.params.is_empty() {
[1284](#1284)            quote! {
[1285](#1285)                #event_name_str => Ok(#enum_name::#variant_name),
[1286](#1286)            }
[1287](#1287)        } else if e.params.len() == 1 {
[1288](#1288)            let (name, _) = &e.params[0];
[1289](#1289)            quote! {
[1290](#1290)                #event_name_str => {
[1291](#1291)                    let (#name,) = event.decode().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1292](#1292)                    Ok(#enum_name::#variant_name { #name })
[1293](#1293)                }
[1294](#1294)            }
[1295](#1295)        } else {
[1296](#1296)            let names: Vec<_> = e.params.iter().map(|(n, _)| n).collect();
[1297](#1297)            quote! {
[1298](#1298)                #event_name_str => {
[1299](#1299)                    let (#(#names),*) = event.decode().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1300](#1300)                    Ok(#enum_name::#variant_name { #(#names),* })
[1301](#1301)                }
[1302](#1302)            }
[1303](#1303)        }
[1304](#1304)    });
[1305](#1305)
[1306](#1306)    let try_from_impl = quote! {
[1307](#1307)        impl TryFrom<&distributed::EventRecord> for #enum_name {
[1308](#1308)            type Error = String;
[1309](#1309)            fn try_from(event: &distributed::EventRecord) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
[1310](#1310)                match event.event_name.as_str() {
[1311](#1311)                    #(#try_from_arms)*
[1312](#1312)                    _ => Err(format!("Unknown event: {}", event.event_name)),
[1313](#1313)                }
[1314](#1314)            }
[1315](#1315)        }
[1316](#1316)    };
[1317](#1317)
[1318](#1318)    let entity_field = &args.entity_field;
[1320](#1320)    let replay_arms: Vec<_> = event_methods
[1321](#1321)        .iter()
[1322](#1322)        .map(|e| {
[1323](#1323)            let event_name_str = &e.event_name;
[1324](#1324)            let method_name = &e.method_name;
[1325](#1325)            if e.params.is_empty() {
[1326](#1326)                quote! {
[1327](#1327)                    #event_name_str => {
[1328](#1328)                        self.#method_name().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1329](#1329)                    }
[1330](#1330)                }
[1331](#1331)            } else if e.params.len() == 1 {
[1332](#1332)                let (name, _) = &e.params[0];
[1333](#1333)                quote! {
[1334](#1334)                    #event_name_str => {
[1335](#1335)                        let (#name,) = event.decode().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1336](#1336)                        self.#method_name(#name).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1337](#1337)                    }
[1338](#1338)                }
[1339](#1339)            } else {
[1340](#1340)                let names: Vec<_> = e.params.iter().map(|(n, _)| n).collect();
[1341](#1341)                quote! {
[1342](#1342)                    #event_name_str => {
[1343](#1343)                        let (#(#names),*) = event.decode().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1344](#1344)                        self.#method_name(#(#names),*).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
[1345](#1345)                    }
[1346](#1346)                }
[1347](#1347)            }
[1348](#1348)        })
[1349](#1349)        .collect();
[1350](#1350)
[1351](#1351)    let (upcaster_wrappers, upcasters_method) =
[1352](#1352)        generate_upcaster_tokens(&struct_name, &args.upcasters);
[1353](#1353)    let aggregate_type_method = args.aggregate_type.as_ref().map(|aggregate_type| {
[1354](#1354)        quote! {
[1355](#1355)            fn aggregate_type() -> &'static str {
[1356](#1356)                #aggregate_type
[1357](#1357)            }
[1358](#1358)        }
[1359](#1359)    });
[1360](#1360)
[1361](#1361)    let aggregate_impl = aggregate_impl_tokens(
[1363](#1363)        &struct_name,
[1364](#1364)        entity_field,
[1365](#1365)        &aggregate_type_method,
[1366](#1366)        &replay_arms,
[1367](#1367)        &upcasters_method,
[1368](#1368)    );
[1369](#1369)
[1370](#1370)    let expanded = quote! {
[1371](#1371)        #impl_block
[1372](#1372)        #enum_def

# aggregate in distributed_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/distributed_macros/2.3.3/distributed_macros/macro.aggregate.html

`aggregate!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

Generates the Aggregate trait impl with replay logic.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
distributed::aggregate!(Todo, entity {
    "initialized"(id, user_id, task) => initialize,
    "completed"() => complete(),
});
```
This generates the `Aggregate` trait impl that handles replaying events.
Events are stored as serialized payloads and deserialized on replay.

Note: Use `=> method()` (with parens) when the method takes no arguments.
Use `=> method` (no parens) to pass all event args to the method.

---

# digest in distributed_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/distributed_macros/2.3.3/distributed_macros/attr.digest.html

`#[digest]`## Expand description

Attribute macro that automatically inserts a digest call at the beginning of a method.

If the annotated method omits a return type, it expands to
`distributed::SourcedResult<()>`. Methods may also explicitly return
`Result<(), E>` where `E` can be constructed from
`distributed::EventRecordError`; explicit `Result` methods should return
`Ok(())` from the original body.

The generated digest call runs before the original method body. This means
serialization errors are returned before the method mutates state. If the
method can reject a command for domain validation reasons, prefer calling
`self.entity.digest(...)?` explicitly after validation and before mutation.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Basic usage with function parameters (automatically captured):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[digest("initialized")]
fn initialize(&mut self, id: String, user_id: String) {
    // digest call auto-inserted, params serialized as tuple
}
```
With guard condition:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[digest("completed", when = !self.completed)]
fn complete(&mut self) -> Result<(), distributed::EventRecordError> {
    self.completed = true;
    Ok(())
}
```
The guard wraps both the digest call and the method body, so a false guard records no event and skips the body.

With validation inside the command body, use explicit digesting:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn rename(&mut self, title: String) -> Result<(), TodoError> {
    if title.trim().is_empty() {
        return Err(TodoError::EmptyTitle);
    }
    self.entity.digest("renamed", &(title.clone(),))?;
    self.title = title;
    Ok(())
}
```
With custom entity field name:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[digest(my_entity, "initialized")]
fn create(&mut self, name: String) -> Result<(), distributed::EventRecordError> {
    // uses self.my_entity instead of self.entity
    Ok(())
}
```
The macro supports:

- Default entity field name: `entity`(can be overridden by specifying field name first)
- `when = condition`: guard that wraps the entire method body

---

# enqueue in distributed_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/distributed_macros/2.3.3/distributed_macros/attr.enqueue.html

`#[enqueue]`## Expand description

Attribute macro that automatically queues a local event for emission.

Similar to `#[digest]`, this macro captures function parameters and
serializes them as the event data (using JSON). Events are queued
during method execution and can be emitted after a successful commit.

**Requires the  emitter feature to be enabled.**

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Basic usage with function parameters (automatically captured):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[enqueue("order.initialized")]
fn create(&mut self, id: String, items: Vec<Item>) {
    // enqueue call auto-inserted, params serialized as JSON
    // calls self.emitter.enqueue_with(...)
}
```
With guard condition:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[enqueue("step.completed", when = self.can_complete())]
fn complete_step(&mut self) {
    self.completed = true;
}
```
With custom emitter field name:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[enqueue(my_emitter, "todo.initialized")]
fn create(&mut self, name: String) {
    // uses self.my_emitter instead of self.emitter
}
```
With a renamed entity field (used for the replay guard):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[enqueue("order.initialized", entity = state)]
fn create(&mut self, id: String) {
    // uses self.state.is_replaying() instead of self.entity.is_replaying()
}
```
The macro supports:

- Default emitter field name: `emitter`(can be overridden by specifying field name first)
- `when = condition`: guard that wraps the entire method body
- `entity = field`: entity field used for the- `is_replaying()`guard (default:- `entity`)
- Methods may omit the return type; the macro expands them to `distributed::SourcedResult<()>`

---

# sourced in distributed_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/distributed_macros/2.3.3/distributed_macros/attr.sourced.html

`#[sourced]`## Expand description

Attribute macro that generates a typed event enum, `TryFrom<&EventRecord>`,
and `impl Aggregate` from annotated methods in an impl block.

Each `#[event(...)]` method is rewritten with the same recording order as
`#[digest]`: event recording runs before the original method body, and a
`when = ...` guard wraps both event recording and the body. Use explicit
`self.entity.digest(...)?` calls for commands that need to validate before
deciding whether to record an event.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[sourced(entity)]
impl Todo {
    #[event("initialized")]
    pub fn initialize(&mut self, id: String, user_id: String, task: String) {
        self.entity.set_id(&id);
        self.user_id = user_id;
        self.task = task;
    }
    #[event("completed", when = !self.completed)]
    pub fn complete(&mut self) {
        self.completed = true;
    }
}
// Generates: TodoEvent enum, TryFrom<&EventRecord>, impl Aggregate
```
Options:

- `#[sourced(entity)]`- entity field name
- `#[sourced(entity, events = "CustomName")]`- custom enum name
- `#[sourced(entity, aggregate_type = "todos")]`- stable stream type name
- `#[sourced(entity, upcasters(("initialized", 1 => 2, OldPayload => NewPayload, upcast_fn)))]`- upcasters

# ReadModel in distributed_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/distributed_macros/2.3.3/distributed_macros/derive.ReadModel.html

```
#[derive(ReadModel)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[readmodel]
    #[collection]
    #[table]
    #[column]
    #[id]
    #[index]
    #[unique]
}
```
## Expand description

Derive macro for the `ReadModel` trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[derive(Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, ReadModel)]
#[collection("counter_views")]
struct CounterView {
    #[id]
    pub id: String,
    pub name: String,
    pub value: i32,
}
```
- `#[readmodel(collection = "...")]`or- `#[collection("...")]`sets the collection name. If omitted, defaults to snake_case struct name + “s”.
- `#[readmodel(table = "...")]`or- `#[table("...")]`opts into relational table metadata.
- `#[readmodel(column = "...")]`or- `#[column("...")]`sets a relational column name.
- `#[readmodel(id)]`,- `#[id]`, or- `#[id("column_name")]`marks the field used as the unique identifier. If omitted, defaults to a field named- `id`.
- `#[readmodel(index)]`,- `#[index]`, or- `#[index("index_name")]`declares a secondary index on a field.
- `#[readmodel(unique)]`,- `#[unique]`, or- `#[unique("index_name")]`declares a unique secondary index on a field.
- `#[index(columns = ["field_a", "field_b"])]`or- `#[index(name = "...", columns = ["field_a", "field_b"])]`declares a compound secondary index on a struct.
- `#[unique(columns = ["field_a", "field_b"])]`or- `#[unique(name = "...", columns = ["field_a", "field_b"])]`declares a compound unique index on a struct.

# Snapshot in distributed_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/distributed_macros/2.3.3/distributed_macros/derive.Snapshot.html

```
#[derive(Snapshot)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[snapshot]
}
```
## Expand description

Derive macro that generates a snapshot struct, `fn snapshot()`, and
`impl Snapshottable` for an aggregate.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[derive(Default, Snapshot)]
struct Todo {
    pub entity: Entity,
    user_id: String,
    task: String,
    completed: bool,
}
```
Generates `TodoSnapshot` with `id: String` + all non-entity fields,
a `fn snapshot()` method, and `impl Snapshottable`.

Options:

- `#[snapshot(id = "sku")]`— use a struct field as the ID key instead of synthesizing- `id`
- `#[snapshot(entity = "my_entity")]`— override the entity field name (default:- `entity`)
- `#[snapshot(version = N)]`— set- `Snapshottable::SNAPSHOT_VERSION`(default: 1). Bump this whenever the snapshot layout changes incompatibly; on load a stored snapshot whose version differs is treated as a cache miss and the aggregate is rebuilt by replay rather than mis-decoded.
- Fields with `#[serde(skip)]`are automatically excluded

# compact_str - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/compact_str/=0.9.0/

## Expand description

`compact_str`

  **A memory efficient string type that can store up to 24* bytes on the stack.**

* 12 bytes for 32-bit architectures

[§](https://docs.rs#about)About

A `CompactString` is a more memory efficient string type, that can store smaller strings on the stack, and transparently stores longer strings on the heap (aka a small string optimization).
It can mostly be used as a drop in replacement for `String` and are particularly useful in parsing, deserializing, or any other application where you may
have smaller strings.

[§](https://docs.rs#properties)Properties

A `CompactString` specifically has the following properties:

- `size_of::<CompactString>() == size_of::<String>()`
- Stores up to 24 bytes on the stack
- 12 bytes if running on a 32 bit architecture

- Strings longer than 24 bytes are stored on the heap
- `Clone`is- `O(n)`
- `From<String>`or- `From<Box<str>>`re-uses underlying buffer- Eagerly inlines small strings

- `O(1)`creation from- `&'static str`with- `CompactString::const_new`
- Heap based string grows at a rate of 1.5x
- The std library `String`grows at a rate of 2x

- The std library
- Space optimized for `Option<_>`- `size_of::<CompactString>() == size_of::<Option<CompactString>>()`

- Uses [branchless instructions](https://en.algorithmica.org/hpc/pipelining/branchless/)for string accesses
- Supports `no_std`environments

[§](https://docs.rs#traits)Traits

This crate exposes two traits, `ToCompactString` and `CompactStringExt`.

[§](https://docs.rs#tocompactstring)`ToCompactString`

Provides the `to_compact_string(&self)` method for converting types into a `CompactString`. This trait is automatically implemented for all types that are `std::fmt::Display`, with specialized higher performance impls for:

- `u8`,- `u16`,- `u32`,- `u64`,- `usize`,- `u128`
- `i8`,- `i16`,- `i32`,- `i64`,- `isize`,- `i128`
- `f32`,- `f64`
- `bool`,- `char`
- `NonZeroU*`,- `NonZeroI*`
- `String`,- `CompactString`

[§](https://docs.rs#compactstringext)`CompactStringExt`

Provides two methods `join_compact(seperator: impl AsRef<str>)` and `concat_compact()`. This trait is automatically implemented for all types that can be converted into an iterator and yield types that `impl AsRef<str>`. This allows you to join Vec’s, slices, and any other collection to form `CompactString`s.

[§](https://docs.rs#macros)Macros

This crate exposes one macro `format_compact!` that can be used to create `CompactString`s from arguments, like you can `String`s with the `std::format!` macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

`compact_str` has the following optional features:

- `serde`, which implements- `Deserialize`- `Serialize`- `serde`- `CompactString`
- `bytes`, which provides two methods- `from_utf8_buf<B: Buf>(buf: &mut B)`and- `from_utf8_buf_unchecked<B: Buf>(buf: &mut B)`, which allows for the creation of a- `CompactString`from a- `bytes::Buf`
- `markup`, which implements- `Render`- `CompactString`s can be used in templates as HTML escaped strings
- `diesel`, which allows using CompactStrings in- `diesel`
- `sqlx-mysql`/- `sqlx-postgres`/- `sqlx-sqlite`, which allows using CompactStrings in- `sqlx`
- `arbitrary`, which implements the- `arbitrary::Arbitrary`
- `proptest`, which implements the- `proptest::arbitrary::Arbitrary`
- `quickcheck`, which implements the- `quickcheck::Arbitrary`
- `rkyv`, which implements- `rkyv::Archive`- `rkyv::Serialize`- `rkyv::Deserialize`
- `smallvec`, provides the- `into_bytes()`method which enables you to convert a- `CompactString`into a byte vector, using- `smallvec::SmallVec`

[§](https://docs.rs#how-it-works)How it works

Note: this explanation assumes a 64-bit architecture, for 32-bit architectures generally divide any number by 2.

Normally strings are stored on the heap since they’re dynamically sized. In Rust a `String` consists of three fields, each of which are the size of a `usize`.
e.g. its layout is something like the following:

`String: [ ptr<8> | len<8> | cap<8> ]`

- `ptr`is a pointer to a location on the heap that stores the string
- `len`is the length of the string
- `cap`is the total capacity of the buffer being pointed to

This results in 24 bytes being stored on the stack, 8 bytes for each field. Then the actual string is stored on the heap, usually with additional memory allocated to prevent re-allocating if the string is mutated.

The idea of `CompactString` is instead of storing metadata on the stack, just store the string itself. This way for smaller strings we save a bit of memory, and we
don’t have to heap allocate so it’s more performant. A `CompactString` is limited to 24 bytes (aka `size_of::<String>()`) so it won’t ever use more memory than a
`String` would.

The memory layout of a `CompactString` looks something like:

`CompactString: [ buffer<23> | len<1> ]`

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-layout)Memory Layout

Internally a `CompactString` has two variants:

- **Inline**, a string <= 24 bytes long
- **Heap**allocated, a string > 24 bytes long

We define a discriminant (aka track which variant we are) *within* the last byte, specifically:

- `0b11111110`- All 1s with a trailing 0, indicates- **heap**allocated
- `0b11XXXXXX`- Two leading 1s, indicates- **inline**, with the trailing 6 bits used to store the length

and the overall memory layout of a `CompactString` is:

- `heap: { ptr: NonNull<u8>, len: usize, cap: Capacity }`
- `inline: { buffer: [u8; 24] }`

Both variants are 24 bytes long

For **heap** allocated strings we use a custom `HeapBuffer` which normally stores the capacity of the string on the stack, but also optionally allows us to store it on the heap. Since we use the last byte to track our discriminant, we only have 7 bytes to store the capacity, or 3 bytes on a 32-bit architecture. 7 bytes allows us to store a value up to `2^56`, aka 64 petabytes, while 3 bytes only allows us to store a value up to `2^24`, aka 16 megabytes.

For 64-bit architectures we always inline the capacity, because we can safely assume our strings will never be larger than 64 petabytes, but on 32-bit architectures, when creating or growing a `CompactString`, if the text is larger than 16MB then we move the capacity onto the heap.

We handle the capacity in this way for two reasons:

- Users shouldn’t have to pay for what they don’t use. Meaning, in the *majority*of cases the capacity of the buffer could easily fit into 7 or 3 bytes, so the user shouldn’t have to pay the memory cost of storing the capacity on the heap, if they don’t need to.
- Allows us to convert `From<String>`in`O(1)`time, by taking the parts of a`String`(e.g.`ptr`,`len`, and`cap`) and using those to create a`CompactString`, without having to do any heap allocations. This is important when using`CompactString`in large codebases where you might have`CompactString`working alongside of`String`.

For **inline** strings we only have a 24 byte buffer on the stack. This might make you wonder how can we store a 24 byte long string, inline? Don’t we also need to store the length somewhere?

To do this, we utilize the fact that the last byte of our string could only ever have a value in the range `[0, 192)`. We know this because all strings in Rust are valid [UTF-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8), and the only valid byte pattern for the last byte of a UTF-8 character (and thus the possible last byte of a string) is `0b0XXXXXXX` aka `[0, 128)` or `0b10XXXXXX` aka `[128, 192)`. This leaves all values in `[192, 255]` as unused in our last byte. Therefore, we can use values in the range of `[192, 215]` to represent a length in the range of `[0, 23]`, and if our last byte has a value `< 192`, we know that’s a UTF-8 character, and can interpret the length of our string as `24`.

Specifically, the last byte on the stack for a `CompactString` has the following uses:

- `[0, 191]`- Is the last byte of a UTF-8 char, the- `CompactString`is stored on the stack and implicitly has a length of- `24`
- `[192, 215]`- Denotes a length in the range of- `[0, 23]`, this- `CompactString`is stored on the stack.
- `216`- Denotes this- `CompactString`is stored on the heap
- `217`- Denotes this- `CompactString`stores a- `&'static str`.
- `[218, 255]`- Unused, denotes e.g. the- `None`variant for- `Option<CompactString>`

[§](https://docs.rs#testing)Testing

Strings and unicode can be quite messy, even further, we’re working with things at the bit level. `compact_str` has an *extensive* test suite comprised of unit testing, property testing, and fuzz testing, to ensure our invariants are upheld. We test across all major OSes (Windows, macOS, and Linux), architectures (64-bit and 32-bit), and endian-ness (big endian and little endian).

Fuzz testing is run with `libFuzzer`, `AFL++`, *and* `honggfuzz`, with `AFL++` running on both `x86_64` and `ARMv7` architectures. We test with [ miri](https://github.com/rust-lang/miri) to catch cases of undefined behavior, and run all tests on every Rust compiler since

`v1.60` to ensure support for our minimum supported Rust version (MSRV).[§](https://docs.rs#unsafe-code)`unsafe` code

`CompactString` uses a bit of unsafe code because we manually define what variant we are, so unlike an enum, the compiler can’t guarantee what value is actually stored.
We also have some manually implemented heap data structures, i.e. `HeapBuffer`, and mess with bytes at a bit level, to make the most out of our resources.
That being said, uses of unsafe code in this library are constrained to only where *absolutely* necessary, and always documented with
`// SAFETY: <reason>`.

[§](https://docs.rs#similar-crates)Similar Crates

Storing strings on the stack is not a new idea, in fact there are a few other crates in the Rust ecosystem that do similar things, an incomplete list:

For a comparison of all these crates (and possibly more!) please see the [Rust String Benchmarks](https://github.com/rosetta-rs/string-rosetta-rs).

Thanks for readingme!

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros-1)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

# htmlize - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/htmlize/=1.1.0/

## Expand description

Htmlize handles both encoding raw strings to be safely inserted in HTML, and
decoding HTML text with entities to get back a raw string. It closely
follows the [official WHATWG spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#character-reference-state) for encoding and decoding text.

```
use htmlize::{escape_attribute, escape_text};
assert!(escape_attribute("ab & < > \" '") == "ab & < > " '");
assert!(escape_text("ab & < > \" '") == "ab & < > \" '");
```
If you enable the `unescape` or `unescape_fast` feature:

`assert!(htmlize::unescape("3 × 4 > 10") == "3 × 4 > 10");`This only deals with HTML entities; it does not add or remove HTML tags.

[§](https://docs.rs#which-escape-function-to-use)Which `escape` function to use

If the text goes in an attribute, use [ escape_attribute()](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_attribute.html), otherwise, use

[. If you need bytes (](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_text.html)

`escape_text()``[u8]`) instead of a `String`, use the
`_bytes` version of the functions: [and](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_attribute_bytes.html)

`escape_attribute_bytes()`[.](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_text_bytes.html)

`escape_text_bytes()`You should almost never need [ escape_all_quotes()](https://docs.rs/fn.escape_all_quotes.html), but it’s included
because sometimes it’s convenient to wrap attribute values in single quotes.

[§](https://docs.rs#which-unescape-function-to-use)Which `unescape` function to use

All `unescape` functions require the `unescape` or `unescape_fast` feature
to be enabled. See the [features](https://docs.rs#features) section below for an
explanation of the trade-offs.

[ unescape()](https://docs.rs/fn.unescape.html) is probably fine for most uses. To be strictly correct, you
should use

[for attribute values.](https://docs.rs/fn.unescape_attribute.html)

`unescape_attribute()`[ unescape_in()](https://docs.rs/fn.unescape_in.html) handles either depending on the value of the

`context`
parameter. See its documentation for a discussion of the differences between
expanding attribute values and general text.[ unescape_bytes_in()](https://docs.rs/fn.unescape_bytes_in.html) is just like

[except that it works on](https://docs.rs/fn.unescape_in.html)

`unescape_in()``[u8]` rather than strings.[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

The `escape` functions are all available with no features enabled.

-
`unescape_fast`: provide fast version of`unescape()`*not*enable the`entities`feature automatically.This takes perhaps 2 seconds longer to build than `unescape`, but the performance is significantly better in the worst cases. That said, the performance of of the`unescape`version is already pretty good, so I don’t recommend enabling this unless you really need it.
-
`unescape`: provide normal version of`unescape()``entities`feature.
-
`entities`: build`ENTITIES`[phf](https://crates.io/crates/phf)and may slow builds by a few seconds.

[§](https://docs.rs#internal-features)Internal features

-
`iai`: enable[iai](https://crates.io/crates/iai)benchmarks. This should only be used when running benchmarks. See the[Benchmarks section in the README](https://github.com/danielparks/htmlize#benchmarks).
-
`bench`: enable unescape benchmarks by making internal functions like`unescape_fast()`public. This must only be used when running benchmarks. It is required to run unescape benchmarks. See the[Benchmarks section in the README](https://github.com/danielparks/htmlize#benchmarks).
-
`_unescape_either`: used internally to configure benchmarks. You should not specify this directly. It is automatically enabled when`unescape_fast`or`unescape`are enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently the minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) is **1.60**. Future
increases in the MSRV will require a major version bump.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- The context for an input string.

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/=1.0.228/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any - `docsrs`
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Deserialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Serialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.

# thiserror - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/thiserror/=2.0.18/

## Expand description

This library provides a convenient derive macro for the standard library’s
[ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/error/trait.Error.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use thiserror::Error;
#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum DataStoreError {
    #[error("data store disconnected")]
    Disconnect(#[from] io::Error),
    #[error("the data for key `{0}` is not available")]
    Redaction(String),
    #[error("invalid header (expected {expected:?}, found {found:?})")]
    InvalidHeader {
        expected: String,
        found: String,
    },
    #[error("unknown data store error")]
    Unknown,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Thiserror deliberately does not appear in your public API. You get the same thing as if you had written an implementation of `std::error::Error`
-
Errors may be enums, structs with named fields, tuple structs, or unit structs.
-
A `Display``#[error("...")]`messages on the struct or each variant of your enum, as shown above in the example.The messages support a shorthand for interpolating fields from the error. - `#[error("{var}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0}")]`⟶- `write!("{}", self.0)`
- `#[error("{var:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.var)`
- `#[error("{0:?}")]`⟶- `write!("{:?}", self.0)`
 These shorthands can be used together with any additional format args, which may be arbitrary expressions. For example: `#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("invalid rdo_lookahead_frames {0} (expected < {max})", max = i32::MAX)] InvalidLookahead(u32), }`If one of the additional expression arguments needs to refer to a field of the struct or enum, then refer to named fields as `.var`and tuple fields as`.0`.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum Error { #[error("first letter must be lowercase but was {:?}", first_char(.0))] WrongCase(String), #[error("invalid index {idx}, expected at least {} and at most {}", .limits.lo, .limits.hi)] OutOfBounds { idx: usize, limits: Limits }, }`
-
A `From``#[from]`attribute.The variant using `#[from]`must not contain any other fields beyond the source error (and possibly a backtrace — see below). Usually`#[from]`fields are unnamed, but`#[from]`is allowed on a named field too.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io(#[from] io::Error), Glob(#[from] globset::Error), }`
-
The Error trait’s `source()``#[source]`attribute or is named`source`, if any. This is for identifying the underlying lower level error that caused your error.The `#[from]`attribute always implies that the same field is`#[source]`, so you don’t ever need to specify both attributes.Any error type that implements `std::error::Error`or dereferences to`dyn std::error::Error`will work as a source.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, #[source] // optional if field name is `source` source: anyhow::Error, }`
-
The Error trait’s `provide()``Backtrace`, if any, as a`std::backtrace::Backtrace``Backtrace`in errors requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`use std::backtrace::Backtrace; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub struct MyError { msg: String, backtrace: Backtrace, // automatically detected }`
-
If a field is both a source (named `source`, or has`#[source]`or`#[from]`attribute)*and*is marked`#[backtrace]`, then the Error trait’s`provide()``provide`so that both layers of the error share the same backtrace. The`#[backtrace]`attribute requires a nightly compiler with Rust version 1.73 or newer.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[backtrace] source: io::Error, }, }`
-
For variants that use `#[from]`and also contain a`Backtrace`field, a backtrace is captured from within the`From`impl.`#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { Io { #[from] source: io::Error, backtrace: Backtrace, }, }`
-
Errors may use `error(transparent)`to forward the source and`Display``#[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum MyError { ... #[error(transparent)] Other(#[from] anyhow::Error), // source and Display delegate to anyhow::Error }`Another use case is hiding implementation details of an error representation behind an opaque error type, so that the representation is able to evolve without breaking the crate’s public API. `// PublicError is public, but opaque and easy to keep compatible. #[derive(Error, Debug)] #[error(transparent)] pub struct PublicError(#[from] ErrorRepr); impl PublicError { // Accessors for anything we do want to expose publicly. } // Private and free to change across minor version of the crate. #[derive(Error, Debug)] enum ErrorRepr { ... }`
-
See also the `anyhow`

# vize_carton - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vize_carton/=0.273.0/

## Expand description

Carton - The artist’s toolbox for Vize.

This crate provides the foundational utilities and data structures for the Vize compiler, much like a carton (artist’s portfolio case) holds all the essential tools and materials an artist needs for their work.

[§](https://docs.rs#modules)Modules

- **Allocator**: Arena-based memory allocation for efficient AST construction
- **Shared utilities**: DOM configuration, optimization flags, and helper functions
- **Telegraph**: Generic message fan-out for report emitters

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use vize_carton::{Allocator, Box, Vec};
let allocator = Allocator::default();
// Allocate a boxed value
let boxed = Box::new_in(42, allocator.as_bump());
assert_eq!(*boxed, 42);
// Create a vector
let mut vec = Vec::new_in(allocator.as_bump());
vec.push(1);
vec.push(2);
vec.push(3);
assert_eq!(vec.len(), 3);
```

- `pub use`- [general](https://docs.rs/general/index.html)::*;

# vize_relief - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vize_relief/=0.273.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#vize_relief)vize_relief

Relief - The sculptured AST surface for Vize. Vue template Abstract Syntax Tree definitions, errors, and compiler options.

[§](https://docs.rs#name-origin)Name Origin

**Relief** (/rɪˈliːf/) is a sculptural technique where figures project from a flat
background, creating depth and dimension. Like how relief carving reveals forms
from a surface, `vize_relief` defines the structural forms (AST nodes) that
represent Vue template syntax.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Complete Vue template AST node definitions
- Compiler error types and codes
- Parser, transform, and codegen options
- Arena-allocated nodes for zero-copy JavaScript interop
- Serialization support with serde

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Code generation AST node types.

- Control flow AST node types.

- Core AST types and enumerations.

- Element-related AST node types.

- Compiler error types and codes.

- Expression AST node types.

- Root and template child node types.
- [options](https://docs.rs/options/index.html)
- Compiler options.
